On June 21, 1961, the disaster was ahead in Vist. The parish church was under renovation and something went crazy. A rooftop worker saw weak smoke development at noon. Shortly afterwards, the entire building was overlit. Of the rich inventories of the church, very little could be saved. by Cnattingius, Bengt, Public Domain Mark (https://www.europeana.eu/item/73/S_OM_photo_OME028238); Museum of Östergötland via Europeana

The Old Church of Åtvid 1917. In 1885 it was decided that the church should be demolished for the benefit of the New Church, inaugurated in the same year. The church decayed but never came to be demolished. After a time of restoration, it came instead to be newly inaugurated in 1957. by Lovén, Lars Fredrik, Public Domain Mark (https://www.europeana.eu/item/73/S_OM_photo_OML000955); Museum of Östergötland via Europeana

In 1927, the Savior wished to build a new local in Norrköping. At the chosen site in the Kapellhorvan district there was an older basement built with a wooden magazine from recent times. This led the Museum of Östergötland to carry out an antiquarian investigation. Ammanuens Bengt Cnattingius describes the basement as erected on the one hand by the split and unworked granite that has been bricked together and trimmed, covered by a barrel vault also made of granite. The mists of the room were 4.25 x 6 m with east-west main direction. As the cellar was not previously judged to have medieval origin, it was acknowledged that it was allowed to be demolished. The picture shows part of the basement facing east. by Cnattingius, Bengt, Public Domain Mark (https://www.europeana.eu/item/73/S_OM_photo_OMNORR000235); Museum of Östergötland via Europeana
